- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next period; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak or use 10-day moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; apply 3-day smoothing to sentiment before weighting forecast adjustments.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >1.5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average to reduce systematic bias.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with cycle phase; match forecast direction to sentiment’s dominant recent trend (not just latest value).
